events.title: Portfolio Workshop
events.description: AI Society’s first workshop is a hands-on session where students turn their resume into a live personal portfolio website using AI tools, with no coding required. We’ll open with a short introduction to AI Society and our plans for the year, then cover how to prompt AI tools effectively. Most of the session is a guided build lab where attendees create, polish and publish their own site with help in the room. We’ll close with a quick demo showcase. Attendees bring a laptop and resume and leave with a shareable link.

events.title: Playground
events.description: Playground × Replit is a hands-on AI building experience bringing Cornell students together to turn ideas into working prototypes. Led by the Replit team, participants will learn how to use AI-powered development tools to build applications, explore creative solutions, and collaborate with fellow students. No prior coding experience is required. The session will feature a Replit walkthrough, an open building session, and informal project demonstrations. Our goal is to make AI-powered product development accessible, encourage entrepreneurship, and help students leave with something tangible they can continue developing.

events.title: Claude Impact Lab at Cornell Tech (Vibe Lab x NYC Claude Community)
events.description: Vibe Lab is partnering with the NYC Claude Community to host a Claude Impact Lab at Cornell Tech. In this free, full-day build event, teams of Cornell Tech students and external builders will work on a real problem from a nonprofit partner, using Claude to build working prototypes and demoing them at the end of the day. Participants get hands-on experience building with AI, collaborate across disciplines, and connect with NYC’s builder community while creating something with real social impact.

events.title: Tech Help @ Cornell Tech
events.description: Every semester, older adult residents of Roosevelt Island visit the Cornell Tech campus with a range of tech support needs (from sending an email to updating their operating system). In response, dedicated students, staff, and faculty (like you!) spend an afternoon providing personalized, one-on-one support. This event not only enhances older adults’ tech skills but also strengthens the relationship between Cornell Tech and the Roosevelt Island community. You can volunteer for as long (or as little) as you want, knowing every bit of help counts. Enjoy complimentary coffee/tea as you work with us!

events.title: Island Editions AAP: Billie Tsien + Cynthia Davidson
events.description: Island Editions is an extraordinary conversation series that invites leading architects to offer candid reflections on their work, the evolution of their careers, and the broader professional and cultural landscapes that shape their thought and practice. Hosted by Cornell AAP faculty members Peter Eisenman (B.Arch ’55) and Cynthia Davidson, the Fall 2026 season features noted architects Preston Scott Cohen (Oct. 26) and Billie Tsien (Dec. 2). Island Editions was launched in Fall 2025 to mark the NYC program’s move to its new permanent home on the 4th floor of the Tata Innovation Center. Previous guests included Bernard Tschumi, Steven Holl, Nader Tehrani, Elizabeth Diller, Toshiko Mori, and J. Meejin Yoon. The series is open to the public. Registration is required.
events.location: Gensler Family AAP NYC Center Tata Innovation Center, 4th Floor; Cornell Tech

event.title: Dealing with Procrastination
event.description:
Hosted by Learning Strategies Center

What exactly is procrastination?
Why does it happen? 
Who is more prone to it? 
How can you deal with it? 

Join Florencia (Flor) Ardon, PhD, Lecturer and Neurodivergent Support Program Manager at the Learning Strategics Center for a conversation around what is - and what is not - procrastination. 

Attendees will be able to clear some misunderstandings, as well as create an action plan that work for them.

event.title: Field Conditions: Incubating Media Arts in NYC
event.description: New York’s art / design / technology field is held together by a coalition between practices and cultural institutions that shape what gets made, who gets supported, and what survives. This panel brings together NEW INC at the New Museum, Rhizome, and Onassis ONX, New York City institutions that have an ongoing commitment to Art, Design and Technology. The conversation will look at how each organization identifies and supports practitioners, where funding and institutional models are heading, and what is actually emerging in practice right now. For anyone working across computational design, interaction, immersive media, and creative technology, it offers a direct view of the infrastructure behind the work and of what it takes to build a practice in this city.

event.title: Revolutionizing Healthcare With AI-Powered Devices
event.description: You are invited to join the Weill Cornell Medicine community for a showcase of digital health innovations and technologies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY, a community-led festival organized by Pulse NYC that celebrates innovation across the AI ecosystem. The following innovators and their AI-enabled technologies will be featured: EmulatRx An agentic AI platform that uses real-world patient data to support clinical trial design. Presented by Weishen Pan, PhD, Research Associate, Department of Population Health Sciences, Weill Cornell Medicine WAV AI An AI-based tool that analyzes sounds to detect fistula stenosis. Presented by Bobak Mosadegh, PhD, Associate Professor of Biomedical Engineering in Radiology and Director, Dalio Institute of Cardiovascular Imaging, Weill Cornell Medicine Postpartum Depression Risk Prediction An Epic-integrated clinical decision support tool that analyzes electronic health record data to identify pregnant patients at elevated risk for postpartum depression. Presented by Yiye Zhang, PhD, MS, Associate Professor of Population Health Sciences, Weill Cornell Medicine Corneal Confocal Microscopy for Neurodegenerative Disease Detection A noninvasive approach that uses corneal confocal microscopy to detect changes in the cornea’s small nerve fibers. Quantitative imaging and predictive analysis may offer an accessible biomarker for detecting and monitoring neurodegeneration. Presented by Rayaz A. Malik, MBChB, PhD, FRCP, Professor of Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine–Qatar We look forward to seeing you there!
